subject: Request: ad-hoc telemetry crosswalk + console query endpoint
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@datawave.io>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: console ad-hoc query for telemetry crosswalk

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the new per-route tiles look promising. We have a tight exec ask at DataWave: our finance and ML teams need to reconcile token-level billing with observed latency distribution across model variants.

Current ask (high level):
- A way to run ad-hoc queries from the console (or an API) that returns token counts, model variant, route id, and per-token compute cost for arbitrary time ranges.
- Ability to join that with our ingestion ids (we've attached a small sample dw_token_sample.csv) so we can crosswalk events back to our records.
- A retention window of 90 days for the raw detail (short-term) and 13 months for aggregated daily snapshots.

Why this matters: finance needs reconciliation for an upcoming audit, and ML wants to identify high-cost chatflows that are producing low quality. Right now we can only see aggregate per-route costs in your console and it's blocking our billing reconciliation.

Can we get a short scope and an ETA for a POC? If a meeting helps I can carve 30m this week. I attached a brief that includes sample queries and the CSV.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Khan
Head of Platform Analytics, DataWave
S: (415) 555-0184

Sara — thanks, this is clear and helpful.

Short answer: we can build a constrained ad-hoc query surface that reads from a normalized telemetry store and exposes token-level rows for a bounded time window. A few things we'll need to align on before committing an ETA:
- exact MVP columns (token_count, model_id, model_variant, route_id, timestamp, cost_token_usd, request_id)
- expected query concurrency and max time-range for interactive queries (e.g., 24h vs 90d)
- RBAC and whether DataWave users will have console access or we surface via a signed query API

Laura — can you and Rafael triage this into the observability backlog? If possible, please provide a rough POC scope and estimate (sprint-based). Rafael, any thoughts on storage/backfill tradeoffs?

Sara — happy to set a 30m sync today or tomorrow to walk through sample queries and the attached CSV. My calendar: 11:30–12:30 or 15:00–16:00 PT.

Diego

Thanks Diego / Sara — I'm Laura, PM for Observability. Quick follow-up with the minimal MVP proposal so engineering can size it: 

MVP surface (console + API):
- Console: lightweight "Query Console" tab under Observability with a pre-populated template: time range, route selector, model variant, aggregation granularity (raw / 1h / daily)
- API: signed ad-hoc query endpoint that accepts JSON with start/end, filters, and returns newline-delimited JSON rows (ndjson)

MVP row schema (minimum):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id
- route_id
- model_id
- model_variant
- token_count (integer)
- token_cost_usd (float)
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)

Retention / sizing:
- raw detail: 90 days (hot store)
- pre-aggregated daily snapshots: 13 months (cold store)

Security:
- signed API keys per customer (short TTL) or console access gated by existing tenant RBAC
- audit log entry for each query (who ran it, when, filters)

SLA targets we need from eng: interactive queries should return within ~3–10s for <48h ranges; larger ranges should stream incremental results. Rafael, can you call out feasibility and a rough timeline (POC vs full)?

Action items:
- Rafael: feasibility, storage options, and estimate (POC = 1–2 sprints?)
- Diego: confirm DataWave's expected concurrency and whether users will use console or API
- Sara: share 2–3 representative queries from your brief (or let us use the CSV)

I'll file OBS-1214 and add this note.

—Laura

Thanks — quick engineering read: technically feasible but there are important cost/latency tradeoffs. Notes below: 

Storage/backfill model:
- Ingest pipeline already emits per-request telemetry; we do not currently store per-token rows persistently (we emit token_count as a field). For the raw detail DataWave wants, we'll need to write per-request rows into a hot store (time-series DB or partitioned parquet on object store + index).
- Backfill for the last 90 days: if DataWave wants full-fidelity from day one, expect a one-time job to rehydrate detail. That is doable but could be large depending on volume.

Query surface proposal (POC):
- POC: nightly ETL that writes a partitioned NDJSON/parquet set for the past 7 days plus an ad-hoc query service that scans partitions with pushdown filters. Use pre-aggregations for daily snapshots.
- Expected POC timeline: 2 sprints (infra + small API), with a follow-up sprint to enable 90d backfill if DataWave opts-in.

Performance constraints and options:
- Interactive SLO: 95th <= 5s for <48h queries if we limit concurrency and use indexed partitions. For larger ranges we'll stream and return incremental pages.
- Cost controls: enable sampling flag (e.g., sample=0.1) and max_rows limit to prevent runaway scans.

Data requirements from DataWave:
- sample of request_ids to match (you provided dw_token_sample.csv — thanks)
- expected concurrent query count (estimate)
- whether tenant users will run arbitrary SQL or we provide constrained filters only

I'll attach a quick token sample that we used while sizing (attached). Once we confirm scope I'll add a more detailed engineering design to OBS-1214.

Rafael Mendes
Engineering Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference
